verify::spawn runs each verification on its own detached thread (std::thread::spawn). The thread builds the Record only after `run` returns: `seq` is next_seq(&dir) and `at` is workspace::now_unix(), both taken at that point, with `elapsed_ms` measured from the thread's start. Then it appends the record to verify.log. So a record's `at`, its `seq` and its position in the log all reflect when its verification finished, not when it started. Two verifications running at once are appended in the order they finish.

note: A verification can itself end `unauthorized`, so a delivered record can carry that status. Inside `run`, a typed leg whose endpoint is missing returns `Err(Status::Unauthorized)` (gate at 1569, classify at 1598), and the test at 5941-5953 asserts that `run` with approach `split` and no typed endpoint returns `Status::Unauthorized` as its overall status, commenting "A wiring fault". Separately, in `block` (958-990), a reply with no delivered record and no started verification is `off` when verification is disabled or the verb is not listed, and `unauthorized` otherwise. `missing` is computed whenever the reply's status equals `unauthorized`, from the *current* settings and keys through `unauthorized_detail`, whether or not that status came from a delivered record.

The rest of `run` (src/verify.rs:1596-1683). Only the classify leg and the check leg end the verification with a non-`ok` status. Each returns immediately on its own failure: `Err(s) => return (s, …)` from typed_classify or `call`, `Unparsable` after parse_assertions or parse_findings fail, and the final `Err(s)` from the check call. The literal and refuter legs run only after the check succeeded. The literal leg's failure becomes `lit_status`, and the refuter "cannot fail the verification", so both end in `(Status::Ok, f, lit_status)`, and both run through `tel`, the same Telemetry the earlier legs wrote `detail` into. The gate leg runs before classify (1559-1575) and records its failure in `tel.gate_status` without ending the run. So on a `timeout`, `unavailable` or `unparsable` record, the last leg to run is the one that failed. On an `ok` record, `detail` may have been written by any leg.

(d) The replay loops for claims (claims.rs:60-80), facts (facts.rs:355-364) and prose (prose.rs:105-120) set `revisions: 0` on Create and add 1 on each Revise event. So a mint's `revisions` is a per-mint counter that only increases, persisted in that verb's own ledger. (e) The three subject constructors, `claim_subject`, `fact_subject` and `prose_subject` (verify.rs:3495-3558), build `Subject { mint, verb, text, evidence }` and set no revision. (f) In checks.rs, grounding is counted only for records whose `proposition_digest` equals the sha256 of the claim's current proposition, or is empty (a record written before digests existed). So after a claim's proposition changes, every grounding record that carries a digest stops counting: "a pass that graded superseded text confirms nothing about this text". Changing only its citations leaves the digest unchanged.
why: Verifier finding: records with an empty proposition_digest still pass the filter, so "count for nothing" overstated.

note: `commit_delivered`'s doc comment (verify.rs 1230-1240) states that nothing serialises the MCP handlers per workspace, so two authoring calls can interleave and both peek the same position. The worst case it names is a finding shown twice.
